title: Hana Savings Bank says outside party breached customer re-verification system; 552 customers' data leaked
date_note: Newsis (24 November) relays the bank's statement; it dates the intrusion to the 16th and customer notification to the 19th, which is outside the map window, so the disclosure day is used.
geo_basis: country named in the source; no city given, pin at Seoul
summary: Newsis reports that Hana Savings Bank said an outside party illegally breached its mobile web customer re-verification system on the 16th and that it confirmed a leak affecting 552 customers. Data includes names, resident registration numbers, phone numbers and addresses, and differs by customer. The bank says it blocked the outside IP address and notified affected customers on the 19th.
plain: Hana Savings Bank says an outside party broke into a customer re-verification system and personal data of 552 customers leaked. The bank says it blocked the outside IP address and told those customers.
exec: A Korean savings bank says 552 customers’ data leaked, including resident registration numbers; the bank warns such data could enable identity theft.
action: As Hana Savings Bank advises, use identity-theft prevention services such as the non-face-to-face account opening block and the loan-transaction safe-block service.

evidence.quote: 고객 552명의 개인(신용)정보가 유출된 정황을 확인했다고 밝혔다.

validation.note: Two independent publishers (Newsis, Herald Business) each report the bank's statement of 552 affected customers and the intrusion into the re-verification system. The bank's own notice was not read. Related: korea-savings-banks-five-hacks-hankyung-2026-11.
